text:
"Connecticut as a Slave State" (By E.B. Bronson 6/17/1916)

"The caste system was in full being in church, business and social life. There was no more question about his right of keeping slaves than of his owning sheep. The minister—the leader and aristocrat of the day—invariably owned his slave or slaves. Even the heavenly-minded John Davenport and Edward Hopkins were not adverse to the custom, and Rev. Ezra Stiles, one time president of Yale college and later a vigorous advocate of emancipation, sent a barrel of rum to Africa to be traded for a 'Blackamoor,' because, he said, 'It is a great privilege for the poor Negroes to be taken from the ignorant and wicked people of Guiana and be placed in a Christian land, where they can become good Christians and go to heaven when they die.' Religious freedom was an inherent right of the mind, but slaveholding was a matter of the pocketbook, and an entirely different proposition in the Puritan eyes. The fact of the matter is, he kept them because it paid.

The high-water mark of slavery in Connecticut was reached in 1774, and thereafter steadily declined. To speak in the Billy Sunday vernacular, 'Connecticut had hit the sawdust path.' The number of slaves rapidly decreased from 6,562 in 1774 to only 2,759 in 1790, and 10 years later, in 1800, there were only 951 slaves in the state. Still the good work went on, and in 1810 only 310 were left. In 1820 but 97, and in 1830, 200 years from the commencement of the evil system, there were only 25 slaves owned within Connecticut's borders. In 1840 there were 17. In 1848 Connecticut experienced a full change of heart and enacted a law forever doing away with this blot upon her fair escutcheon, and emancipated all slaves remaining in Connecticut. At this time there were but six slaves remaining in bondage within the state."Throughout the whole history of this slavery thraldom in Connecticut, some curious laws were passed, showing that the Puritan was not fully satisfied with the situation. In 1702, there was enacted a law which arose from the practice of turning loose a slave who had broken down, and was of little use, and abandoning him, thus forcing him to care for himself. This law obliged the last owner of the slave and his heirs, and administrators, to pay for the care of these wrecks of humanity. In 1711 it was further enacted, that in case the former owner refused to give the care required, the selectmen of the town where the owner resided, should care for the needy slave, and collect with costs from his owner. 

In 1774 it was enacted that 'no Indian, Negro, or mulatto slave, shall at any time hereafter be brought or imported into this state, by sea or by land, from any place or places whatsoever, to be disposed of, left or sold, within this state. In 1784, a law was passed which provided that no Negro or mulatto child born after March 1, 1784, should be held in servitude beyond the age of 25 years. In 1797, a further enactment released all colored children from slavery, when they 'had attained the age of 21 years.' Connecticut gradually was 'coming to her own' again. Even the ministry received a change of heart, for in 1788, the general association of ministers of Connecticut declared the slave trade to be unjust, and that every justifiable measure ought to be taken to suppress it. In 1789, Connecticut shippers were prohibited from engaging in the slave trade anywhere.

One of the interesting points to note in this gradual metamorphosis is that as the number of slaves gradually diminished, the number of free Negroes correspondingly increased, showing that but comparatively few left the state. The caste system was in full force everywhere. It was very evident in the church. For years the system of 'dignifying the pews,' as it was termed, was practiced. That is, assigning seats to the different members of the parish by a committee appointed for that purpose. For a man must go to church whether he wished to or not, and pay his share of supporting the minister, by a tax laid upon him and collected by the town. Social standing secured the first choice of seats, wealth the second, and piety the last. In this assignment one or more pews were 'set off' away up in the top of the gallery for the slaves of the social leaders and ministers. At the First Congregational church, Winsted, there were two pews thus 'set off' in the gallery, and they were so high up that they were called 'Nigger heaven.'"In 1837, a number of enthusiasts were invited to meet in Wolcottville (now Torrington) to organize a county abolition society. Upon looking for a place of meeting, they found that every church, public and private hall, was closed against them, and also heard public threats of violence if they persisted in attempting to hold a meeting, from the proslavery element of the town. A barn was offered them as a meeting place and promptly accepted. The barn was filled, floor, scaffold, haymow and stables, by these disciples of abolition. It was a very cold day in January, and much suffering resulted in spite of their warm zeal. Roger S. Mills of New Hartford was appointed chairman, and Rev. R. M. Chipman of Harwinton secretary, and Daniel Coe of Winsted offered prayer. The following officers were appointed: President, Roger S. Mills; vice-presidents, Erastus Lyman of Goshen, Gen. Daniel Brinsmade of Washington, Gen. Uriel Tuttle of Torringford and Jonathan Coe of Winsted; secretary, Rev. R. M. Chipman of Harwinton, and treasurer, Dr. E. D. Hudson of Torringford. While being addressed by an agent of the American society, and suffering from extreme cold, they were attacked by a mob of proslaveryites who had paraded the streets of Wolcottville and had elevated their courage with New England rum. They gathered around the barn which was near the Congregational church, yelling, blowing horns, thumping on tin pans and kettles, and ringing furiously the church bell, and finally, by brute force, broke up the meeting which took a hasty adjournment."When the people were leaving Wolcottville the entire village seemed to be a bedlam. Dea Ebenezer Rood was set upon while in his sleigh, and some of the mob endeavored to overturn him and cause his horses to run away. But the blood of his Puritan ancestors became rampant, and in defiance he shouted: 'Rattle your pans; hoot and toot; ring your bells, ye pesky fools, if it does ye any good,' and plying his whip to his now frantic horses he escaped the mob.

Torringford street arose in its anger and might, at this insult, opened her church doors, and the abolition convention held session there for two days. Although there was great opposition on the street at this new move, there was no other demonstration."Inspired by Dea Rood's defiance, the abolition spirit blazed high, and monthly meetings were held in barns, sheds, and groves, throughout the county. These enthusiasts were called all sorts of opprobrious names such as, 'Nigger friends, and disturbers of Israel,' and some were excommunicated from the churches. These were indeed stirring days; Connecticut had received a change of heart, and in her ecstasy had forgotten her own sins.

Even our own village did not escape unscathed. A pastor of the First Congregational church who had strong antislavery principles, dared to preach an abolition sermon one Sunday from his pulpit, and the next morning the village was flooded with a 'Broadside' demanding the people to rise, and teach this disturber a lesson, and not allow such sins to be perpetrated in their midst. A copy of this sheet was even nailed upon his own doorway, and is now deposited in our historical society, and is worthy of your perusal."Even the historic cannon now reposing in our historical rooms was used to break up 'pestilent abolition meetings' in our own midst. Thus I have endeavored to give you some idea of an interesting phase in the history of our Commonwealth, that may not be familiar to all, and which I would term as a Connecticut mistake."
—The Springfield Republican, June 18, 1916.

text:
Where the Heart Follows the Light

Where the wild Atlantic meets Galloway’s rugged shores,
and the salty wind bends the grasses along the cliffs,
the evening sun settles gently over the sea,
casting its golden light across the weathered stones,
while Corsewall Lighthouse stands quietly against the sky,
a familiar landmark for those finding their way.

There’s something about this corner of Scotland
that makes me want to slow down,
pull my jacket a little tighter against the breeze,
and follow the coastal path simply to see where it leads.

And somewhere in that wandering,
my imagination drifts to a certain Scotsman,
with unruly curls, thoughtful blue eyes,
and a smile that suggests he enjoys a good laugh.

I can picture an ordinary sort of afternoon,
walking along the coast,
stopping to admire the lighthouse,
perhaps sharing a funny story
or debating which direction offers the better view.

There might be muddy boots,
wind-tangled hair,
and a few moments when conversation gives way
to the sound of waves against the rocks.

Nothing extravagant.
No grand romantic gestures,
no promises written in the stars.
Just the pleasant thought
of good company in a beautiful place.

Of course, it’s only a daydream,
inspired by a familiar face
and a landscape I’d love to experience for myself.
The real person has a life beyond my imagination,
and the real coastline has its own beauty,
whether anyone walks beside me or not.

Still, there’s no harm in letting a little imagination
add warmth to an ordinary afternoon,
so long as I remember
that the loveliest part of the dream
may simply be the place itself.

And perhaps one day,
I’ll stand along the Rhins of Galloway,
feel that Scottish wind against my face,
watch the lighthouse brighten as evening falls,
and smile at how a photograph
once inspired such a lovely little story.

Because sometimes a daydream
doesn’t need to become a romance
to mean something.

Sometimes it simply reminds us
that there are beautiful places to discover,
interesting people to meet,
and real adventures still waiting
just beyond the next bend in the path.

text:
Long before Charlie Murphy became known to millions for his unforgettable stories on Chappelle’s Show, he was simply Eddie Murphy’s older brother, a close family member who was also finding his own way in the entertainment world. This photo captures the two brothers during the height of Eddie’s rise in the 1980s, when he had already become one of the biggest young stars in comedy.

Charlie’s path was very different from Eddie’s. Born in Brooklyn in 1959, he served six years in the U.S. Navy before returning to civilian life and eventually pursuing comedy, writing and acting. He also worked closely with Eddie during the early years of his career, including serving as part of his brother’s security and entourage. Charlie later made his feature film debut alongside Eddie in Harlem Nights in 1989 and contributed writing to projects including Vampire in Brooklyn and Norbit.

Charlie eventually became a major comedian in his own right. His breakthrough with a wider audience came through Chappelle’s Show, where his hilarious retellings of encounters with celebrities such as Rick James and Prince became some of the most remembered sketches in the show's history. What made Charlie especially memorable was his storytelling. He could take an experience from decades earlier and turn it into a story that felt completely alive.

Charlie Murphy died from leukemia in 2017 at the age of 57. Today, photographs like this offer a glimpse at the brothers before Charlie became a household name himself, and before Eddie's career would become one of the most influential in modern comedy and film.

text:
LAKE FOREST, Calif. — Witnesses say masked federal agents fired less-lethal projectiles at people documenting an immigration operation—including a minor child m.

Videos show armed ICE agents confronting community members—while photographs confirm their injuries.

The morning immigration enforcement operation at an Orange County shopping center turned into a heated confrontation between heavily armed federal agents and community members.

The incident happened November 1 in the parking lot of Lake Forest Village, near Muirlands Boulevard and Ridge Route Drive.

Several videos recorded by people at the scene show masked agents in tactical gear standing near unmarked vehicles while community members film them, demand identification, and question their actions.

Photographs shared afterward show injuries to two individuals—including circular reddish marks on one person's back and a round, dark-red mark on another person's upper abdomen.

One of the most serious accusations involves a minor who was allegedly shot in the chest. According to the activist organization Stop ICE Alerts, an agent laughed when confronted about the child's injury.

"You just shot a minor, how do you feel?" a community member reportedly asked.

"It felt great," the agent allegedly replied.

Other social media accounts have described the agent's response as "That was amazing."

The claims are accompanied by two photographs showing the injuries.

One photograph shows a person's exposed upper back with a reddish circular area near the shoulder blade and a separate smaller mark lower on the back—close to a clothing strap.

The second photograph shows an individual lifting a gray shirt to reveal a sharply defined circular mark on the upper abdomen or lower chest. The center of the mark appears darker, with surrounding reddish discoloration.

No medical records, hospital statements, or independent examinations of the injuries have been made publicly available.

As of Monday evening, November 2, no major Southern California news outlet appeared to have published an incident-specific report, and no official explanation from Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the Department of Homeland Security, or the Orange County Sheriff's Department had been issued to the public.

The initial alert claimed the agents had already detained at least one person before community observers arrived. However, a later update from a moderator of the same reporting network said the agents departed around 11:20 a.m. and that no abduction had been reported at that location.

Another report published at 1:30 p.m. alleged that agents had taken someone into custody around 11:30 a.m. and refused to identify themselves.

Those conflicting accounts leave it unclear whether anyone was detained at the shopping center.

Additional recordings capture people shouting at agents, demanding their badge numbers and questioning why they were carrying weapons.

"Sons of bitches, he has got a gun," a bystander reportedly shouts in one of the recordings.

Another person declares, "I'm a fucking citizen."

Witnesses say the confrontation escalated when an agent carrying a less-lethal weapon fired projectiles toward community members.

The large black device visible in portions of the footage appears consistent with a pepper-ball launcher, a compressed-air weapon that fires specialized projectiles. Many such devices use approximately .68-caliber ammunition containing powdered chemical irritants.

Pepper-ball projectiles can cause painful impacts, bruising, and other injuries even when they do not penetrate the skin. Although classified as less-lethal, they can cause serious harm, particularly when fired at vulnerable areas of the body.

Stop ICE Alerts initially described the agents as firing rubber bullets, although other accounts specifically identify pepper balls.

The organization alleged that community members had simply gathered to document the agents as they usually do.

One disputed claim involves a bystander allegedly touching or striking the window of an ICE vehicle before force was used.

There is no verified official account establishing whether that striking occurred, what kind of contact may have taken place, or whether it had any connection to the reported deployment of projectiles.

The footage was first amplified on X through @LongTimeHistory, which posted a full-length and credited recording with a complete list of known details about the allegations and reported injuries.

The X account @CantStopPoppin circulated shorter clips of the confrontation, including recordings approximately 47 seconds and 94 seconds long.

An X post from @KimKatieUSA offered a different interpretation, emphasizing that people had approached and confronted the agents—and arguing that the particular recordings being shared did not show officers firing weapons.

The allegation concerning the agent's reported reaction to shooting a minor has drawn some of the strongest criticism online.

According to Stop ICE Alerts, a community member directly confronted an agent about the child's reported injury and asked how he felt about it.

The organization claimed that the agent laughed before answering, "It felt great."

Other accounts circulated a slightly different version of the remark, using the words "That was amazing."

Another major source of frustration involved the agents' identities.

In several recordings, people can be seen and heard demanding that masked personnel provide names and badge numbers.

One agent carrying what appears to be a pepper-ball launcher responded that he did not need to provide his badge number.

An Orange County Sheriff's Department deputy subsequently arrived. Witnesses claim that the deputy also refused repeated requests for a badge number.

One witness questioned why deputies were not checking the identification of masked federal agents.

Another person said that they were able to identify one sheriff's deputy by name. Public records indicate that an employee with that name has worked for the department.

Orange County Sheriff Don Barnes has previously emphasized that his department does not independently enforce federal immigration law.

"The Orange County Sheriff's Department does not enforce federal immigration law," Barnes said in a January 2025 statement.

The sheriff has nevertheless defended forms of cooperation with federal authorities that are permitted under existing law, particularly involving individuals already in county custody.

For now, the November 1 confrontation leaves residents with questions that have become increasingly familiar during recent immigration operations in Orange County:
Who was detained, why were heavily armed agents present, what prompted their use of force, and what happens when people trying to document federal operations say they were injured by the very officers they were recording?

text:
Apropos of nothing, I want to post my spiel about if-then commitments.

IIRC, that term originally comes from one of those very important 30-author Bengio-Hinton “AI risks are a big deal” papers they used to publish in 2023, but I’m mostly familiar with it because of some articles written by Holden Karnofsky, deservedly renowned poster/thinker/EA/Anthropic guy. 

Like a lot of great ideas, it’s pretty simple. An AI company says “If one of our models has capability X, we will undertake mitigation Y, and if we can’t do mitigation Y we will pause development/deployment until we can.”

I think this is a good and important idea. But, very obviously, if-then commitments only work if there’s some sort of external leviathan that can enforce the commitment. Otherwise it doesn’t work, because the company is incentivized to commit to whatever results in good PR and warm fuzzy feelings at time A and then defect and refuse to honor the commitment at time B. *Making* the commitment is easy and profitable; *honoring* the commitment is difficult and costly. Words are just words, and two trillion dollars is an amount of money that has a mind of its own and makes its own decisions. I’m no Holden Karnofsky, but if someone offered me a billion dollars to stop believing something there’s a part of me that thinks I would probably fold immediately.

Karnofsky knew this, of course. His Carnegie piece about if-then commitments has a whole discussion of how, ultimately, these voluntary commitments are only going to work if they get turned into legally binding government regulations. Otherwise it’s the frog and toad meme, right? You can put the cookies in the box, but that doesn’t stop you from having more cookies because future you can always just open the box. Some external force has to bind the company to the mast; otherwise, the incentives will do what incentives do.

But when SB 53 said “okay, we the state of California are an external leviathan and we will now enforce any commitments you make in your Responsible Scaling Policy,” Anthropic’s response was to create a new RSP that didn’t commit to anything. So now they have one RSP that they are legally obligated to comply with that commits to nothing, and another RSP that they pinky promise to comply with that commits to lots of fun safety stuff. Their revealed preference is to do whatever they want to do at any given time.

And when Anthropic introduced a bill, everything in the bill was totally voluntary. They have to publish and comply with a safety framework; the safety framework will be written by their compliance lawyers, in such a way as to minimize liability. They have to hire an independent auditor to verify that their models aren’t about to kill lots of people; they can pick whoever they want, and fire them at will, and the government has no authority to license or oversee auditors, and the auditor’s findings have essentially no consequences unless the government can prove in court that a catastrophe is imminent.

This doesn’t look like a company that wants to bind itself to the mast. 

That said, I firmly believe that this happened because someone goofed up, and that Anthropic will shortly send many impossible-to-fake costly signals of their good faith by supporting strong state and federal safety legislation.

text:
THAT $75 MEAL IS NOW A $100 MEAL. THE PERCENTAGE DIDN'T NEED A RAISE. 🧾

An LA restaurant reportedly threatened to BLACKLIST six customers for questioning an automatic 18% gratuity. Six people who couldn't even sit at the same table. Two tables, two servers, one large-party fee anyway.

"Okay, we won't charge you this time, but next time you cannot come here, we'll blacklist you."

Blacklist me, Chad. Please. Put my name on the wall. Do it in neon.

I'm done pretending this is normal. Let's talk about the screen.

You know the screen. You flip it around, and it's already loaded: 20%, 22%, 25%. Three buttons, and the smallest one is bigger than the standard tip used to be. The "custom" option is in gray 8-point font at the bottom, positioned like a confession booth.

And the kicker? It's calculating off the TOTAL. Including tax. You're tipping the server on the money that goes to the state of California. Gavin Newsom did not refill your water.

Here's how I tip, and I've tipped this way since 1998:

🍴 15% on the food. PRE-TAX.
🍸 5% on the alcohol. Pouring a glass of wine is not the same labor as carrying four plates.
🚫 0% on tax. Not my tax. Not your tip.

On a $100 pre-tax bill that's half food, half booze, that's $10.

And before anybody clutches their apron, here's the whole scale:

⭐ Great service: 20% on the food. Same rules. Still 5% on the booze, still nothing on the tax.
👍 Average: 15%.
👎 Below average: 10%.
🚩 Rude? A conversation with your manager, and the math gets very simple.

I have never once shorted a server who hustled. Not once. Earn the 20, and it's yours.

Now here's the part nobody wants to say out loud.

The percentage NEVER needed to change, because the percentage was already an automatic raise.

In 1998, a nice dinner ran $40. The same meal today runs about $98, per federal restaurant price data. Food away from home is up 145% since then.

At a flat 15%:
📆 In 1998: that tip was $6.00
📆 Today: that same tip is $14.70

That's a 145% raise. For the same job. For carrying the same plates the same thirty feet. Nobody asked the server to work harder, and inflation did the negotiating.

So when the industry says 15% isn't enough anymore, what they mean is 145% wasn't enough. They want the raise AND the percentage bump AND the tax included AND a mandatory fee if you show up with friends.

And now the tip is tax-advantaged on top of it. The new law lets tipped workers deduct up to $25,000 of reported tips from federal income tax through 2028. I'm fine with that. I like it. But let's not pretend that $14.70 is the same as $14.70 of taxable wages.

Here's my offer, and it's a good one:

Do your job well, and you get the 20. Simple.

But I'm not funding a 25% default on a taxed total because a tablet guilt-tripped me while you stood there watching.

And if the arithmetic is too hard, we live in the future. Set up a @grok prompt on your phone, snap a picture of the receipt, and let the AI do it: 20% of the food pre-tax, 5% of the alcohol, zero on the tax. Takes four seconds. We have robots landing rockets on boats. You can split a dinner check.

And if that gets me blacklisted from a restaurant, honey, that's not a punishment. That's a coupon. 🦋

Gold Movie

Gold is a 2016 American epic crime drama film directed by Stephen Gaghan and written by Patrick Massett and John Zinman. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Édgar Ramírez, Bryce Dallas Howard, Corey Stoll, Toby Kebbell, Craig T. Nelson, Stacy Keach and Bruce Greenwood. The film is loosely based on the true story of the 1997 Bre-X mining scandal, when a massive gold deposit was supposedly discovered in the jungles of Indonesia; however, for legal reasons and to enhance the appeal of the film, character names and story details were changed.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Gold Movie

Gold is a 2016 American epic crime drama film directed by Stephen Gaghan and written by Patrick Massett and John Zinman. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Édgar Ramírez, Bryce Dallas Howard, Corey Stoll, Toby Kebbell, Craig T. Nelson, Stacy Keach and Bruce Greenwood. The film is loosely based on the true story of the 1997 Bre-X mining scandal, when a massive gold deposit was supposedly discovered in the jungles of Indonesia; however, for legal reasons and to enhance the appeal of the film, character names and story details were changed.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
NFL Week 8 Review ✍️

My thoughts on all the games (entering Monday) with statistical analysis, upgrades, and downgrades for each team. Thank you for reading.

Packers 27, Panthers 19 (TNF)
Green Bay won the box score (+1.6 net YPP, +13.5% net SR) but lost TOs (2-3). They were great on 3rd downs (9/16) and in the RZ scoring TDs on all 3 possessions. Bryce Young looked small in the pocket, even smaller than usual, and took 6 sacks. His offensive line didn’t do him any favors. Carolina had their lowest YPP mark of the season 93.7) and have posted negative EPA on early downs for two straight weeks. Whatever goodwill this offense garnered early in the season has been totally eroded. They are struggling to run it and unless Young plays above his pay grade I just don’t see this team winning many games. Green Bay has shown steady improvement on offense and should get Micah Parsons back at some point. Jordan Love can be explosive and leads all qualifying QBs in air yards. The Christian Watson injury was weird and they definitely need him to remain dangerous on the outside. If he stays healthy I think the Packers are a buy down the stretch. Slight upgrade Green Bay. Slight downgrade Carolina.

Cardinals 33, Cowboys 30 (OT)
Insane game that included Dallas blowing a 24-10 lead in the 4th quarter, a game-tying drive in the final minute, and a missed XP to force OT. Arizona dominated YPP (6.2 to 3.7) but slightly lost SR (39.4% to 38.7%). The Cardinals also lost TOs (0-2) and benched Jacoby Brissett for Gardner Minshew who dominated in the 4th quarter (14/16, 166 yards, 3 TDs). Jeremiyah Love sustained another leg injury but Tyler Allgeier had 191 scrimmage yards and 2 TDs on 16 touches including a 63-yard touchdown run and a 52-yard rush. Mike LaFleur named Minshew the new starting QB going forward. Based on my experience watching him, he is better in spot duty and in short spurts, but his play eventually tails off after multiple games as the starter. Maybe LaFleuer will have better luck with him in the long term. Either way it will be a fun watch. The Cowboys continue to be a very easy handicap. They will beat the teams who struggle to move it against their horrific defense but when they face an offense that can match their level they will likely lose in back-and-forth shootouts. Their win over the Eagles last week continues to age like milk. Big downgrade Dallas. Slightly smaller upgrade Arizona.

Bucs 16, Falcons 0
Tampa won the box score (+2.2 net YPP, +13.6% net SR) and also won TOs (4-1) in a rainy slopfest. Micahel Penix Jr. had no ability to throw the football in the rain. Make a mental note of that for whenever he plays his next game outdoors in bad weather. Baker Mayfield only attempted 3 passes and didn’t complete a single one. It was the first time an NFL team won without completing a pass since Buffalo in 1974. Insane stat. The Bucs ran the piss out of it for 324 yards on 56 carries and completely shutdown the Falcons run game. I had a feeling Tampa would rally around Baker Mayfield who has a personal vendetta against Kevin Stefanski for how he was treated in Cleveland. The Bucs defense is now #1 in EPA per play allowed and have not had a below average defensive performance all season. They are a legit threat to win the NFC South and my over 8.5 regular season win total bet which I almost used as toilet paper after an 0-5 start is very much alive at 3-5. Meanwhile Atlanta is a team that lacks consistency and balance. If they can’t generate explosive runs with Bijan they are a very flat offense. I give them some grace here because of the conditions, but they are trending down. Slight downgrade Atlanta. Slight upgrade Tampa.

Bills 36, Ravens 10
Buffalo dominated the box score (+2.7 net YPP, 16.3% net SR) and won TOs (3-2) but there really isn’t much to analyze here because of the fluke QB injuries. Lamar Jackson got hurt on the Ravens first play from scrimmage. Then Tyler Huntley got hurt later in the first half. That meant emergency QB Joe Fagnano got thrust into action. He played as well as you would expect an undrafted rookie from UConn to play in his first NFL action. It was one of the ugliest performances I’ve ever seen at the QB position. The Ravens defense kept them somewhat within striking distance until the dam finally broke midway through the 3rd quarter. There’s only so much the defense can do when you are that limited on offense. Derrick Henry only had 11 carries and Zay Flowers had zero catches. The Bills pass rush was effective. Josh Allen played good but not great. DJ Moore suffered an injury in the 2nd half which is something to keep an eye on going forward. I think Buffalo is the best team in the AFC right now despite some issues on defense. Obviously they weren’t challenged in this game but that will be something to watch out for when they face a real offense. No upgrade or downgrade for either team. I already have Buffalo at the top of my ratings and I don’t think they deserve a bump for this game. I need to wait and see what the Ravens do at QB before I decide how to handle their rating. Obviously I will downgrade them, the question is how much. I’m hearing some rumblings about Tyson Bagent. Personally I would love to see a Joe Flacco reunion. Regardless of who they bring in I think it’s possible you’ve seen the last of Lamar Jackson in a Ravens uniform. This injury looks like a season-ender and the team has an out after the 2027 season. I think that situation will be a hot button topic this offseason.

Steelers 27, Browns 6
Pittsburgh won the box score (+1.1 net YPP, +3.7 net SR) and won TOs (2-1). They also sacked Deshaun Watson eight times and completely overwhelmed the Browns offensive line. This was the first time all season a team has returned from Europe and played well the following week. Prior to this game teams in that situation were 0-8 SU and 1-6-1 ATS when returning from Europe and playing the following week without a bye. Those trends are fun to talk about, but I don’t think they are very predictive. Plenty of other factors need to be accounted for. First of all, Cleveland beat Pittsburgh earlier this season, and it’s rare to sweep a divisional opponent, especially in this matchup. The Browns haven’t swept the Steelers in the regular season since 1988. I expected Pittsburgh to be fully up for this game and they were. What I didn’t expect was Cleveland to look completely flat on both sides. The Steelers dominated the ground game. Jaylen Warren had 17 rushes for 8.4 yards per carry and 108 yards after contact. Aaron Rodgers hasn’t been very accurate or efficient this season, but he understands what the defense is showing him and attacks accordingly. Pittsburgh is getting back to the style of play which made them successful in prior decades which is dominating both lines of scrimmage. The Steelers rank 3rd in EPA per designed rush allowed and 1st in EPA per designed rush this season. I think the Browns will continue to struggle against the more physical teams on their schedule. The one bright spot was TE Harold Fannin Jr. who went off for 153 yards on 10 catches and 12 targets. He was a beast at Bowling Green and its clearly translating to the NFL. Not to be outdone, TE Darnell Washington also had 94 receiving yards on just 3 catches including a 58-yard explosive. He might be the biggest mismatch in the league right now at 6-foot-7. This was an elite TE game. Slight downgrade Cleveland. Slightly bigger upgrade Pittsburgh.

Jaguars 42, Colts 7
Belt to ass. Jacksonville won the box score (+2.7 net YPP, +5.6 net SR) and won TOs (3-1). The Colts looked completely outclassed and lost 34.89 combined EPA to turnovers, sacks, and penalties. Daniel Jones threw 2 INTs one of them was returned 92 yards for a TD when the Colts were driving in the RZ. Anthony Richardson got some run in the 4th quarter and killed my Jones pass attempts over prop. This game was total annihilation. I don’t want to overreact to Jacksonville’s performance because Indy looks like a complete dead stick after trading away their best offensive and defensive lineman last week. I think Jonathan Taylor will be next. Several teams are aggressively pursuing him and whoever lands him will get an elite back in his prime on a relatively team-friendly contract (2 years, $44 million). Meanwhile the Jags look like a balanced team (3rd in EPA per play on offense, 5th on defense) they play in a weak division with a soft schedule down the stretch. Their game this Thursday at Baltimore just got a lot easier and then they play the Titans twice in the next four weeks. They have a legit chance to be the No. 1 seed in the AFC if Buffalo or Denver slips up. Big downgrade Indy. Slightly smaller upgrade Jacksonville.

Raiders 38, Jets 33
The Jets won the box score (+1.4 net YPP, +0.8% net SR) but lost TOs (0-1) and gave up the first kickoff return for a TD in the NFL all season to a 6th-round journeyman RB Dylan Laube who is from Long Island. Great moment for him in a homecoming game but just unacceptable considering the circumstances of the game. Kirk Cousins played well and the Jets defense had no answer for the Raiders TEs who combined for 145 yards receiving and 2 TDs. RB Braelon Allen was a bright spot with 8 carries for 81 yards and an 87.5% success rate on shotgun runs. I don’t think there is a team in the NFL with a wider gap between talent on the field and lack of talent in the coaching box than the Jets. This is a legitimately good roster with talented receivers, a pair of solid backs, a stout offensive line, and an experienced QB that can deliver the football with accuracy and verticality, but Aaron Glenn adds zero value on the sidelines. The Raiders continue to play soft on defense and will struggle when teams can make adjustments on how to defend the tight ends. They don’t have a legit weapon on the outside to keep defenses honest and their run game is inconsistent. Cousins is fine but offers no mobility if the play breaks down outside the pocket. It sounds like he will continue to start until the Raiders are out of the playoff race, and this win just extended that leash by at least another few games. The Raiders play the Niners, Seahawks, Broncos, and Browns over the next four weeks and will be underdogs in all four games. If Vegas is 4-8 heading into their bye in Week 13 I think Mendoza has a chance to start the Week 14 game against the Chargers. That would be a soft landing spot for him. Slight upgrade Vegas. Slight downgrade Jets only because of their complete lack of polish. This roster is actually talented enough to compete but they are severely hamstrung by the culture. I would like to see Aaron Glenn fired but not sure it will happen before the end of the regular season. If they do fire him midseason, I think Frank Reich should get a shot to be the interim head coach.

Lions 19, Vikings 15
Detroit won the box score (+1.4 net YPP, +1.8 net SR) and TOs were even (1-1). Minnesota’s defense did a good job holding down the Detroit offense in the first half, but the Lions exploded in the 2nd half with a 92nd percentile rushing success rate. The Vikings also missed 12 tackles in the 2nd half compared to just 3 in the first half. Jahmyr Gibbs went off for 153 rushing yards and 116 in the 2nd half. The Lions had the highest explosive play rate in a game against the Vikings in the Brian Flores era. They had 10 rushes of at least 10 yards and finished the game with 230 on the ground. On the other side, the Vikings offense has yet to clear the 50th percentile in EPA per play all season. It’s obvious that Kyler Murray is not the answer. Considering the Lions soft defense and the explosive weapons on the outside for Minnesota you would think Kevin O’Connell would be much more aggressive with his gameplan. Well Murray only attempted 29 passes, his 2nd lowest mark of the season. You can usually tell how much a coach trusts his QB by the types of plays he calls. I believe the lack of aggressiveness in this game is a major red flag. It was clear Justin Jefferson was also getting frustrated with Murray in the 2nd half. I wonder if KOC is regretting his decision to ship J.J. McCarthy out of town. Maybe they go to Carson Wentz. Who knows. The Lions continue to live on the knife’s edge which is where Dan Campbell seems to thrive. They have been on the right side of two coinflips against divisional opponents the last two weeks.  Stacking divisional wins is important considering how tight the NFC North is at the top. I think the Lions are a solid playoff team but I don’t think they are good enough to beat the teams out west. We likely won’t find out the answer to that question until the playoffs. Minnesota feels like a fringe playoff team at best despite their 6-0 start. They play the Bills, Packers, and Niners the next three weeks. Yikes. Slight upgrade Detroit. Slightly bigger downgrade Minnesota.

Bengals 43, Titans 36 (OT)
Fun game. Cincinnati won the box score (+1.0 net YPP, +7.7 net SR) but lost TOs (2-4). Joe Burrow had a Jameis Winston type of line with 462 passing yards, 5 TDs and 3 INTs. Tee Higgins had 10 catches on 11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns. He produced the third highest total receiving EPA among this season’s qualifying performances. Ja’Marr Chase also had 11 catches for 141 yards and a touchdown. Credit Cam Ward who played perhaps the best game of his career. I thought the game was over in the 4th quarter after the Bengals took a 29-28 lead. But Ward marched them down the field to pull back in front and even got the 2-point conversion to put them up 7. Credit Burrow for not flinching but it’s fair to say he got outplayed by Ward in this game who did not commit a turnover on the road and only took 2 sacks. I think Cincinnati was clearly looking past this Tennessee team based on how soft they played defensively. They let the Titans jump out to a quick 13-0 lead before waking up in the 2nd quarter. Perhaps they were looking ahead to their looming trip to Spain. The thing about bad teams like the Titans is they will show you glimpses of greatness, they are professionals after all, but then struggle to string together consistent performances week to week. I would be willing to bet the Titans offense comes crashing back down to earth against the Jags this week. No upgrade or downgrade for either team. The Bengals were lucky to escape with a win but credit them for making the plays when they needed to late in the game. I expect them to play much better, especially on defense, against the Falcons in Spain before returning home for a huge primetime game against the Steelers in two weeks which could decide the AFC North.

Rams 24, Chargers 9
The Rams won the box score (+0.2 net YPP, +17.7% net SR) and won TOs (2-1) but I didn’t think they played that well, especially on offense. Matthew Stafford is starting to look his age and has shown inconsistencies under pressure. Obviously he was never much of a mobile QB anyways, but he looks particularly flustered by pressure this season. It doesn’t help that DaVante Adams and his best TE weapons are out, but it’s something to keep an eye on when things get tougher against better teams later this season. The Rams defense was gifted a couple of Justin Herbert meatballs. I honestly think he is the most disappointing player in the league right now when you consider his talent and expectations. I have no idea how to fix this Chargers offense. They can’t run it, they can’t throw it, they have a horrific offensive line and Herbert looks like he is seeing ghosts. I don’t think they will fire Mike McCarthy midseason because I don’t believe he is the issue with this team. If they keep losing games they will have a chance to draft Jeremiah Smith who might be the best WR prospect I’ve seen since Julio Jones. They also need a ton of help on the offensive line. The schedule makers did the Rams a favor by giving them the return matchup against the Niners and both Seahawks games in the final five weeks of the season. Perhaps the Rams will be fully healthy by then and we will see their best stuff. The run game continues to keep things afloat. Blake Corum and Kyren Williams are in a true timeshare. Puka is their only consistent weapon on the outside until Adams returns. It also sounds like Terrance Ferguson and Myles Garrett will be returning soon. Slight upgrade Rams. Much bigger downgrade Chargers. Herbert is lost right now and I don’t see this getting better anytime soon. I’ve now dropped them over 7 points from the start of the regular season. Yikes.

Patriots 24, Dolphins 19
New England won the box score (+1.2 net YPP, +9.0% net SR) but TOs were even (1-1) and a sluggish start made this game appear closer than it actually was. Miami led 13-3 at half and I thought maybe the Pats were suffering from a severe case of the South Beach flu, however they rallied in the 2nd half and Drake Maye showed you his ceiling. When he doesn’t turn it over he is one of the better QBs in the league at navigating the pocket and finding his receivers deep down the field. He also scored a sweet TD in the RZ on a read-option keep. The Dolphins stayed within the number thanks to a late TD throw from Malik Willis on a busted coverage. This offense still doesn’t scare me if you can shut down the run game, which New England did for the most part. I had a feeling the Dolphins offense would come back to Earth after their explosion in the first half off the bye against the Jets last week. If the Pats didn’t sleepwalk through the first half of this game they probably cover easily. So New England winning but not covering was probably the right result. The Pats offense didn’t miss AJ Brown much, however the Hunter Henry injury is something to keep an eye on as he is their most effective TE weapon. I wonder if Mike Vrabel is regretting the Brown trade. Karma says that was never going to workout considering the circumstances behind it and the Russini drama this offseason. No upgrade or downgrade for either team.

Broncos 28, Chiefs 24
Kansas City won the box score (+0.7 net YPP, +6.4% net SR) but got outplayed in the 4th quarter. Credit both teams for playing a clean game with no turnovers. I thought the Chiefs were going to win this game going away until Denver woke up late. Jonah Coleman looks like the real deal, not only as a runner but also a receiver. I mentioned him in last week’s writeup and it’s clear that he has taken full control of the RB1 job. Bo Nix was solid but not spectacular. He continues to play steadily and does a good job avoiding big mistakes. The Chiefs offense looked sharper with Rashee Rice back in the mix but Kenneth Walker got bottled up for a second straight game. Emmett Johnson had 121 of his 128 yards come after the catch and he will likely keep getting chances, especially on special teams. The Chiefs defense completely collapsing in the 4th quarter is the one red flag for me. Or maybe it’s just Mile High magic. The Broncos never seem to be out of it. Hard to kill. They are very solid in the trenches. I love their defense which continues to generate pressure at a high level and has one of the best cover corners in the league. If they ever get safety Talanoa Hufanga back they will be even better. They are also really good on the offensive line and only allowed a 5.7% pressure rate in this game. I think the Chiefs will be fine after two straight losses against two quality opponents. They have some nice bounce back spots over the next three weeks against the Jets, Falcons, and Cardinals. Slight upgrade Denver. Slight downgrade Kansas City.

Commanders 27, Eagles 10 (SNF)
Washington won the box score (+2.0 net YPP, +1.7% net SR) and won TOs (2-1). The Commanders got off to a sluggish start off the bye with some unforced errors which led to a quick 10-0 lead for Philly, however once Jayden Daniels got rolling the field was tilted in their direction. The Eagles have now lost six straight games and haven’t gained over 320 yards since their Week 2 comeback win over the Titans. Saquon Barkley is gutting out through multiple injuries but seems to make things worse with each carry. Tanner McKee is a statue in the pocket and there are limited weapons on the outside with DeVonta Smith out. Makai Lemon looks like a solid receiver but it’s tough to ask a rookie to carry the load with a backup QB and a limited run game. The defense meanwhile looks completely overwhelmed and got embarrassed in the second half for the second straight week in primetime against a divisional opponent. I don’t love this Commanders team but we will learn a lot more over the next three weeks with games against the Rams, Giants, and Bengals. Slight upgrade Washington. Slightly bigger downgrade Philly. I don’t think we have found their floor quite yet.

text:
Curtis Hertel talks about party unity. His actions tell a rather different story.

Haley Stevens wasn't some political newcomer. She helped rescue GM and Chrysler and save more than 200,000 Michigan jobs as Chief of Staff to Obama's Auto Rescue Task Force. She flipped a Republican-held congressional seat in 2018, served Michigan in Congress and helped Democrats build their electoral strength nationally.

After losing the primary, she accepted the result, pledged to support El-Sayed and tried to make unity work. Yet the relationship deteriorated, she was excluded from the planned unity event, and her support was effectively rejected. When she finally endorsed Rogers, Hertel piled on.

"Who cares what Haley Stevens thinks?" was his response.

He then declared her no longer a member of the Michigan Democratic Party and said she had no future in it.

On whose authority? Where is the formal party decision? Was there a vote? What process was followed? A party chairman's public declaration is not, by itself, proof of a formal expulsion.

And who does Hertel think he represents? Not himself, not El-Sayed and certainly not an inherited Lansing political network. He represents a party whose members and voters have a right to expect more than leadership-enforced loyalty.

Hertel's own family is deeply embedded in Michigan politics: his father was a House co-Speaker, his brother is a state senator, other relatives have held political office, and his wife heads Michigan's Department of Health and Human Services.

That is a considerable concentration of political and public-sector influence.

Stevens helped build the party, win seats and save Michigan jobs. She tried to offer unity after defeat. Now the party chairman publicly writes her out of the organisation.

Where is the big tent? Where is the respect for the voters who elected her? And since when does the chairman get to decide, by public pronouncement, who belongs in the Democratic Party?

text:
I Am Palestinian… Who Are You?!

They asked me: Who are you? What is your identity? And who do you represent? My answer deserves to be spoken with pride and dignity:

I am Palestinian. Who could ever truly describe me? I am the son of thyme and olive trees, the son of a land watered by the blood of my ancestors, whose roots have been deeply embedded in history long before Balfour and his infamous declaration.

I carry in my soul the majesty of Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, in my blood the spirit and defiance of Gaza, which refuses to compromise, and in my heart the story of a homeland that never dies and a right that can never be erased by forgetfulness or the passage of time.

I am the son of a land that has never bowed before the storms, and the son of a people who have learned to turn pain into hope, rubble into determination, and siege into steadfastness.

From this land, I inherit the authenticity of belonging; from history, I inherit pride; and from dignity, I inherit a status that no measure can diminish.

I am the Palestinian who has never granted anyone the right to dispose of his homeland, nor authorized anyone to surrender its soil, history, or identity. I am not a stranger passing through this geography, nor a guest upon this land. I am its son, and it is my identity, my home, and the very extension of my existence.

I come from a people who have offered martyrs, prisoners, and wounded heroes. Wars have driven them from their homes, yet they have never allowed Palestine to be driven from their memories.

Homes may be demolished, trees uprooted, and crossings closed. Thirst and hunger may be imposed upon us, and political maps and projects may be forced upon us. But no one can uproot our belonging to our homeland or confiscate our right to freedom and independence.

I am the Palestinian who believes that Jerusalem is not merely a city; it is a capital, a cause, a homeland, a historical conviction, and an identity. And Palestine is not a piece of land open to bargaining, nor a passing humanitarian issue to be reduced to aid packages or shelter tents.

Our rightful claim, as a people and as the owners of a just cause, is to an independent Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital; a state governed by the will of its people, safeguarding the dignity of its citizens, protecting their rights, restoring to the displaced their right to return to their homes, and opening the doors of hope for generations whose childhoods and dreams have been stolen.

I am the name that God keeps alive and protects. I am the son of a history that has yet to be fully written, and the son of a future that will never be confiscated. I am the bearer of the story, the rightful owner of the cause, and the voice of the land when the world falls silent.

I may grow weary. I may break beneath the weight of pain. I may lose my home, my family, and my loved ones. But I will never lose my homeland, Palestine.

So, it is time for you to know who I am!

I am Palestinian…

The one born from the womb of suffering, raised on the love of the land, and destined to carry the key of return and the olive branch until the dawn of freedom breaks and the flag of Palestine flies over its land, with Jerusalem as its capital.

This is who I am… This is my identity… This is my belonging… And this is my pledge and my right, a right that shall never expire with the passage of time.

Abdullah Omar🇵🇸✌️

text:
Detroit helped imagine the future through sound.

Techno’s roots in the city are about more than machines making a dance beat. The MSU Museum describes the genre as a platform for Black voices responding to cultural change and imagining new futures, closely connected with Afrofuturism.

In 2025, the museum explored that history in an exhibition featuring a 45-minute sound installation by Underground Resistance and video work by Detroit artist Andrew Charles Edman. It brought a musical movement into conversation with the city’s industrial landscape, identity and community.

That exhibition has ended, but its online account offers a good way into the subject. Listen with those ideas in mind and a familiar electronic rhythm can become a record of place, experimentation and possibility.

Michigan’s music history contains many different futures dreamed up by local artists. What Detroit track would you choose to introduce someone to techno?

Read the exhibition archive: https://t.co/ibFBMzWnyL
